summary: Indicators agree with the headline: no VAT boxes for an unregistered trader, tax charged on a positive taxable profit, capital allowances match the capitalised spend, and the profit bridge residue is zero. Only minor notes on the nil personal allowance and the unsettled debtor balance.

concerns.why: Consistent with taper at £226,508 income, but worth a glance that the allowance is deliberately nil rather than unpopulated.
Debtors exceed the year's sales; explained by the stated opening balance and no settlements recorded, so behavioural rather than wrong.

severity.where: Self Assessment (SA103S) section vs Profit & Loss Account expense lines
severity.why: The SA103S breakdown does not obviously map to the P&L lines (P&L cost of sales £10,540 plus direct costs £8,000; expenses of £57,452 against only £26,438 analysed on the return). Net profit and taxable profit agree, so this looks like a grouping/mapping difference rather than a missing journal, but the allocation between SA103S boxes should be checked.

For an IT consultancy with no payroll, motor costs of £7,598 and an unanalysed "Other Expenses" figure of £17,882 (the largest single expense) are plausible but worth a look — the "other" bucket being the biggest cost is unusual and may indicate codes that should sit in a named line.
